This suit is filed by the plaintiffs against the defendants for partition and separate possession of their 1/5th share each in the suit item Nos.1 to 13.
2.

The brief facts of the case of plaintiff is that:-
The plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3 are the Members of Joint family governed by Hindu Mithakshara Law.
The suit properties are the joint family property.
The first defendant who is now deceased had two wives by name Rajamma, she is no more and Rathnamma - the defendant No.2.
Rajamma is the mother of defendant No.3, the defendant No.2 is the mother of plaintiffs.

The plaintiffs contended that the joint family consisting of plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3 owned and possessed Sy.No.47/1 measuring 1 acre 25 guntas, Sy.No.116 measuring 2 acres, Sy.No.51/5 measuring 32 guntas and one gramatana site O.S.No.6424/2013 which are situated at Gollahalli village, Uttarahalli Hobli,
Bengaluru South Taluk.
The plaintiffs stated that they and defendant Nos.1 to 3 are in joint possession and enjoyment of the said properties.

The plaintiffs stated that in Sy.No.47/1, measuring 1 acre 25 guntas, Sy.No.116, measuring 2 acres and Sy.No.51/5 measuring 32 guntas were acquired by Bengaluru Development Authority in the year 2003-04 for formation of Anjanapura Layout.
The compensation amount was awarded in the name of first defendant and two sites have been allotted and registered in the name of the first defendant as incentive sites.

The plaintiffs stated that the defendant No.1 is managing the family as kartha, he colluded with the defendant Nos.2 and 3 mismanaging the joint family properties and the amount received from Bengaluru Development Authority as compensation amount.
Therefore, the plaintiffs are intended to separate from the joint family, they approached the first defendant in the month of April 2013 insisted the defendant No.1 to effect the partition in the joint family.
The first defendant refused to give the legitimate share.

The plaintiffs stated that out of the compensation amount, the first defendant has purchased property bearing No.29, assessment No.62/2, katha No.2, now comes under BBMP limit, totally measuring 120375 sq.ft by virtue of Sale Deed, dated 25-06-2014 from R.Suresh and others in the name of defendant No.2.

The first defendant without having the exclusive right, title or interest over the item Nos.5 to 12 property, sold those properties in favour of defendant Nos.4 to 25 which Padma vs Krishnappa M on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191101590/
6 is not binding on the shares of the plaintiffs.
The plaintiffs stated that item Nos.5 to 12 properties are the joint family properties of plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3.
The first defendant has no absolute and salable interest over the item Nos.5 to 12.
The BDA has allotted the sites in the name of first defendant for the benefit of entire family.
Therefore, the plaintiffs prays to decree the suit and award 1/5th share each to the plaintiffs in the suit schedule properties.

They have also sought to declare the Sale Deeds executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant Nos.4 to 25 in respect of item Nos.5 to 12 are not binding.
3.
The suit summons issued to the defendants.
The defendant Nos.12, 14, 25 are placed exparte.
The remaining O.S.No.6424/2013 defendants appeared through their counsel.
Among them, the defendant Nos.4 & 11 have filed the written statement.
They contended that the suit filed by the plaintiffs is false and vexatious, it is filed in collusion with the defendant Nos.1 to 3.

The defendant Nos.4 & 11 categorically denied the plaint averments in toto and they stated that the defendant Nos.4 to 11 before purchasing the item Nos.5 to 12 made thorough enquiry and after having been convinced by the title of the first defendant and also the say of the first defendant that he is selling the sites in favour of the defendant Nos.4 to 11 for the legal and family necessity opted to purchase the same.

The defendants contended that the defendant No.1 has used the sale consideration amount for the welfare of the family, the plaintiffs and other defendants have benefited by the sale and acquisition of the land.
The defendant Nos.4 & 11 have also filed additional written statement denying the contents of amended plaint, para Nos.6(a) to (c).

They contended that the land Sy.No.47/1 measuring 1 acre 25 guntas, Sy.No.51/5, measuring 1 acre 5 guntas are acquired by the BDA for formation of Anjanapura Layout, those properties are self O.S.No.6424/2013 acquired properties of the first defendant.
He has got every independent right to deal with the properties.
Therefore, they prayed to dismiss the suit.

4. Based on the pleadings, my Predecessor has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the plaintiffs prove that suit schedule properties are the joint family properties of themselves and defendants?

My findings to the above issues are as follows:-
 Recasted Issue No.1 : Negative  Issue No.2 : Negative  Recasted Issue No.3 : Affiramtive  Issue No.4 : Negative  Addl. Issue No.1 : Negative  Issue No.5 : As per final order for the following  REASONS 9. Issue Nos.1 to 3:-
Since these issues are in respect of the existence of joint family and joint family properties.

Among the defendants only, the defendant Nos.4 to 11 have filed the written statement,
they have not disputed the family tree.
The relationship between the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3 is not denied by the O.S.No.6424/2013 defendant Nos.4 to 11.
In plaint averments, as well as in the family tree, the plaintiffs stated that the first defendant was their father, he had two wives.
The first wife is Rajamma.
After the death of Rajamma, the first defendant married with second defendant.
The third defendant is daughter of Krishnappa and his wife Rajamma.

10. The plaintiffs claimed that Sy.No.47/1 measuring 1 acre 25 guntas Sy.No.118 measuring 2 acres,
Sy.No.51/5 measuring 32 guntas, one Gramatana site are the joint family properties of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3.
It is admitted fact that all the lands referred above are acquired by BDA for formation of Anjanapura Layout, and extended Anjanapura layout.
It is also not in dispute that the defendant Nos.4 to 24 are the purchasers of the item Nos.5 to 12.
But the case of the plaintiffs is that these defendants have purchased the properties during the pendency of this suit.
Therefore, the transactions made by the defendant Nos.4 to 25 are hit by lis pendency.
The majority of the documents produced by the plaintiffs and defendants are remained undisputed.
11. The plaintiffs relied upon the acquisition proceedings, Sale Deed of he defendant No.1, the Sale Deed of defendant Nos. 5 O.S.No.6424/2013 to 25 in support of their case.
Ex.P.1 is the Power of Attorney executed by the plaintiffs in favour of P.W.1.
Ex.P.2 is the demand register in respect of the suit item No.3.
Ex . P.3
is the Judgment and award passed in LAC No.146/2004 filed by Archana and others.
Ex.P.3 is one of the material document to ascertain the nature of land Sy.No.47/1 of Gollahalli village.

12. According to the case of the plaintiffs, this land is the joint family property, whereas, the defendant Nos.4 to 11 contended that al the land Sy.No.47/1, 51/5 and 118 measuring 2 acres are not the joint family properties.

In Ex.P.3 at page No.6, the Presiding Officer of XII Addl.City Civil &
Sessions Judge's Court clearly observed that the land Sy.No.47/1 measuring 1 acre 25 guntas purchased by Krishnappa by virtue of Sale Deed.
In para No.11 of the Judgment, it is clearly mentioned that Krishnappa has purchased 1 acre 25 guntas from Narayanappa and Munibyrappa.

Therefore, the Court awarded the compensation of 1 acre 25 guntas of land in favour of defendant No.1, who is the father of plaintiffs and defendant No.3.
Ex . P.10

marked in LAC 146/2004 is marked as Ex.P.4, wherein, it is clearly mentioned that Sy.No.47/1 measuring 1 acre 25 guntas purchased by the first defendant from Munibyrappa and O.S.No.6424/2013 Narayanappa by virtue of sale deed,
dated 27-7-1972.
On the date of purchase of the property, the plaintiffs might not have born even the defendant No.3 might not have born or if she is born, she is very young in age.
13. The claim of the plaintiff is that it is the joint family property.
In order to treat the land Sy.No.47/1 as joint family property, there must be other properties or the defendant No.1 has treated this property as joint family property.
There is no pleadings in this respect.
14. Further, it is not the case of the plaintiffs that this land is purchased by the first defendant out of the joint family income or out of the income of ancestral property.
There is no single word in the plaint that there are ancestral properties derived by the first defendant and out of the income from the ancestral property, this land Sy.No.47/1 is purchased by them.

Therefore, the land Sy.No.47/1 becomes the joint family property at the hands of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3.
15.

Apart from it, Ex.P.4 clearly reveals that this land is purchased by the first defendant before the birth of the plaintiffs and O.S.No.6424/2013 during the minority of the defendant No.3, there are not iota of evidence to sow that there are ancestral properties which fetches income.
In the absence of proof regarding the existence of joint family fund, the acquisition of land Sy.No.47/1 is the self acquisition of the first defendant.
Ex. P.5
is the encumbrance certificate, it shows that 1 acre 25 guntas standing in the name of the first defendant from 1989 to 2003.
Exs. P.7
to P.9 are the mutation extracts and tax paid receipts, those clearly goes to show that the first defendant got mutated his name to land Sy.No.47/1 and 51/5.
Exs. P.12
to P.26 are the Sale Deeds executed by the defendant No.1, defendant No.4 to others.
There are multiple transactions took place in respect of suit item Nos.4 to 12.
After acquisition of the land Sy.No.47/1, the BDA has also acquired another land belonging to the plaintiffs situated in Sy.No.51/5, Gollahalli Village for formation extended the Anjanapura layout.
The defendants have produced the entire transactions of land acquisition in respect of Sy.No.51/5 measuring 1 acre 5 guntas.
Those documents are marked as Exs.D.1 to D.47.
The material and important documents is that this land Sy.No.51/5 is also the self acquired property of first defendant.
. The defendants produced Ex.D.36 to show that Sy.No.51/5 was purchased by Krishnappa from Munibyrappa and Narayanappa.
It was acquired by the BDA as per the proceedings marked as Ex.D.1.
At the initial stage, the first defendant has not claimed the award amount.
Therefore, the Special LAO deposited the awarded amount before the City Civil Court and sent reference under Section 30 & 31 of Old Land Acquisition Act.
Subsequently, the first defendant claimed the amount and award was passed in LAC No.151/2003.

While delivering the Judgment and award, the learned XII Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge, in page No.4 of the Judgment stated that Sy.No.51/5 of Gollahalli Village measuring 1 acre 5 guntas purchased by deceased Krishnappa the defendant of this case.
The Sale Deed is marked as Ex.P.1 in the said LAC case.

sentences.text: After acquisition of this land, some of the sites have been allotted to the first defendant as per the incentive scheme of BDA.
Those sites have been sold by defendant No.1 during his life time in favour of defendant Nos.5 to 25 of this case.

17. The plaintiffs have again failed to produced any iota of evidence to show that Sy.No.51/5 is purchased by first defendant O.S.No.6424/2013 out of the joint family nucleus and there is existence of joint family on the date of purchase of this property.
As per Ex.D.38 Sy.No.51/5 was purchased by Krishnappa on 12-06-1961.
By the time, the plaintiffs or the defendant No.3 were not born.
It is also not borne from the records that the marriage between the first defendant and second defendant was also not performed.
During the life time of Krishnappa, she never considered these two lands as joint family property.

Further, during his life time itself, these two lands are acquired by BDA regarding Sy.No.118, regarding 2 acres there is one RTC which shows that it is also acquired by the BDA but the details of acquisition, details of grant of compensation in respect of this land is not mentioned.

18. Further, there is no iota of evidence to show that item Nos.1 to 4 properties are also the joint family properties. No adjoining house owners, the family members are examined by the plaintiffs to prove that their father Krishnappa acquired item Nos.1 to 4 out of ancestral property or joint family fund.
By the time of filing of the suit, the first defendant was alive.

He has not filed any written statement admitting the claim of the plaintiffs or he has not denied the transactions made by him in selling the suit item Nos.5 to 12.
O.S.No.6424/2013
There is no iota of documentary evidence in respect of item No.13 to show that it is also liable for partition.
19. Ex.P.28 is the Sale Deed which is produced to show that site No.296 is allotted to Krishnappa by the BDA in lieu if acquisition of Sy.No.51/5.
So also, Ex.P.29 is the Sale Deed of site No.295 executed by the BDA in favour of Krishnappa.
The plaintiffs have not stepped into the witness box.
They examined their Power of Attorney holder.

P.W.1 stated that the plaintiffs are illiterate lady,
thereafter, they gave power of attorney in favour of him.
20.
In para No.2, page No.13 of the cross-examination, he admitted that the land Sy.No.47/1 measuring 1 acre 25 guntas, Sy.No.55/1, measuring 1 acre 8 guntas of Gollahalli Village.

Sy.No.118 measuring 2 acres of Kenchanapura Village acquired by BDA and in the formation of compensation,
the item Nos. 5 to 12 are allotted to the first defendant.

Those Sale Deeds are marked as Exs.P.37 to P.44.
21.

According to the learned counsel for the plaintiff, all these Sale Deeds are took place during the pendency of the suit but by the O.S.No.6424/2013 time these Sale Deeds are executed there is no any injunction order operating against the defendant Nos.4 to 25.
Moreover, at the time of filing of the suit, only the suit item Nos.1 to 4 are included.
The defendant Nos.4 to 25 and item Nos.5 to 13 are subsequently impleaded by virtue of order on I.A.Nos.2 and 3.
These applications are filed on 4-7-2014.
By that time, there was no stay was operating.
The defendant Nos.12 to 25 were added on the order of order passed by this Court on I.A.No.6 till then, they are not aware of the proceedings.

sentences.text: This decision is referred by the advocate for defendant Nos.4 to 11 stating that the plaintiffs are the daughters of second wife of first defendant.
They are legitimate children.
During the life time of he first defendant, they have filed the suit.
The suit properties are the self acquired property of first defendant.
Therefore, the suit is not maintainable.

But, in the plaint and evidence affidavit of P.W.1,
it is mentioned that after the death of his O.S.No.6424/2013 first wife, Rajamma, the first defendant married with second defendant.
Therefore, question of illegitimacy does not arise.
But the fact is that in the absence of documentary evidence, it can be safely inferred that all the suit properties are self acquired properties of the first defendant.
Item Nos.5 to 12 allotted to the first defendant under the incentive scheme.
Those are already alienated by the first defendant in favour of the defendant Nos.4 to 25.
There is no positive evidence regarding item Nos.1 to 4 and 13 that these are also liable for partition.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In order to treat the land Sy.No.47/1 as joint family property, there must be other properties or the defendant No.1 has treated this property as joint family property.
14. Further, it is not the case of the plaintiffs that this land is purchased by the first defendant out of the joint family income or out of the income of ancestral property.
There is no single word in the plaint that there are ancestral properties derived by the first defendant and out of the income from the ancestral property, this land Sy.No.47/1 is purchased by them.
Therefore, the land Sy.No.47/1 becomes the joint family property at the hands of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3.
15.
It was acquired by the BDA as per the proceedings marked as Ex.D.1.
At the initial stage, the first defendant has not claimed the award amount.
Therefore, the Special LAO deposited the awarded amount before the City Civil Court and sent reference under Section 30 & 31 of Old Land Acquisition Act.
Subsequently, the first defendant claimed the amount and award was passed in LAC No.151/2003.
The defendant Nos.4 to 25 and item Nos.5 to 13 are subsequently impleaded by virtue of order on I.A.Nos.2 and 3.
Therefore, doctrine of lis pendency is not applicable.
The suit properties are the self acquired property of first defendant.
But the fact is that in the absence of documentary evidence, it can be safely inferred that all the suit properties are self acquired properties of the first defendant.
Item Nos.5 to 12 allotted to the first defendant under the incentive scheme.
The plaintiffs failed to prove that any of the suit property acquired by the first defendant out of the O.S.No.6424/2013 joint family or with the aid of ancestral property.
During the life time of first defendant, he never considered any suit properties as the joint family properties.
Therefore, the plaintiffs are not entitled for any share in the suit properties and the suit properties are not the joint family properties of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 to 3.
24.
The plaintiffs sought for declaration that the Sale Deeds executed by the first defendant in favour of defendant Nos.4 to 25 in respect of item Nos.5 to 12 properties are not binding but there is no specific prayer sought by the plaintiffs in the prayer column of the plaint.
In the Sale deeds of item Nos.5 to 11, there is clear reference that the sale is made for legal and family necessity.
